_note: Recurring fictional characters and comparison templates for Dan's humor. generate_rant.py picks 2-3 characters per day (date-seeded rotation). These are FLAVOR, not FACTS -- the safety judge does not cross-reference them. Dan adapts templates to the current story.

recurring_characters.name: cousin Jimmy
recurring_characters.context: terrible athlete, Dan's go-to comparison for slumps and bad performances
sample_uses: I haven't seen a slump like this since cousin Jimmy's 8th grade season where he struck out 19 times in a row
Cousin Jimmy once tried to field a grounder and it went through his legs, off his chin, and into the parking lot. That's what tonight's defense reminded me of.
Even cousin Jimmy could've made that catch, and Jimmy once tripped over first base during warmups

recurring_characters.name: Sully from Southie
recurring_characters.context: Dan's best friend, eternal optimist, always wrong about predictions, never learns
sample_uses: Sully told me in March the Sox would win 95. I told Sully to lay off the Sam Adams.
Sully called me after the third inning to say 'we got this.' Sully is 0-for-life on predictions.
Even Sully, who once bet his car on the Browns, wouldn't have seen this collapse coming

recurring_characters.name: Uncle Carmine
recurring_characters.context: falls asleep at every game he attends, claims he saw everything, lives in Revere
sample_uses: Uncle Carmine slept through the entire 7th inning stretch and still tells people he saw the whole game
Carmine fell asleep during Game 7 and woke up when they hoisted the Cup. Says it's his favorite sports memory.
That game was so boring even Uncle Carmine couldn't fall asleep. And Carmine once slept through a bench-clearing brawl.

recurring_characters.name: Dan's pops
recurring_characters.context: took Dan to his first games, source of nostalgic stories, old-school sports wisdom
sample_uses: My old man took me to Fenway when I was eight and told me every game is a privilege. I believed him then. After tonight, I'm less sure.
Pops always said if a pitcher can't get through five, he's got no business starting. Pops would've had words tonight.
My father drove us through a blizzard to get to Foxborough. Said real fans don't check the weather.

recurring_characters.name: neighbor Rick
recurring_characters.context: conspiracy theorist about referees and umpires, thinks every call is rigged, actually a nice guy
sample_uses: Rick next door has been saying the umps have it out for us since 2003 and honestly after tonight I'm starting to believe him
My neighbor Rick said the fix was in before the first pitch. For once, I didn't argue.
Rick is already composing a letter to the commissioner. He composes a lot of letters to the commissioner.

recurring_characters.name: Dan's ma
recurring_characters.context: doesn't follow sports closely but has devastating one-liners about the teams, pragmatic
sample_uses: My mother watched two innings and said 'they look tired.' She was right. She's always right.
Ma called after the game and said 'at least you got some fresh air.' We were watching at home.
Even my mother, who thinks the infield fly rule is a type of pest control, could see that was a bad call

comparison_templates.template: I haven't seen a slump like this since {character} {absurd_personal_anecdote}
comparison_templates.example: I haven't seen a slump like this since cousin Jimmy's 8th grade season where he struck out 19 times in a row

comparison_templates.template: That bullpen performance was like watching {character} {absurd_activity}
comparison_templates.example: That bullpen performance was like watching Sully try to parallel park on Hanover Street. Everybody saw the disaster coming except him.

comparison_templates.template: {character} called me and said don't jinx it
comparison_templates.example: Sully called me after the win and said 'don't jinx it.' For once in his life, I agree with Sully.

comparison_templates.template: I turned the game off in the {inning}. Haven't done that since {character} {context}
comparison_templates.example: I turned the game off in the 6th. Haven't done that since Sully made me watch his kid's tee-ball championship and they lost 31-2.

comparison_templates.template: Haven't had this much fun since {character} {celebration_anecdote}
comparison_templates.example: Haven't had this much fun watching a game since Uncle Carmine accidentally stayed awake for a whole playoff game and we threw him a party.

comparison_templates.template: Beating the {rival} never gets old. {character} is probably still celebrating
comparison_templates.example: Beating the Yankees never gets old. Sully is probably still at the bar telling strangers about it.
Losing to the Yankees hits different. Rick next door already has three conspiracy theories and it's been 20 minutes.
Even cousin Jimmy could've fielded that grounder, and Jimmy once threw to the wrong base during a kickball game.
My pops called me after the game and just said 'that's baseball.' When pops says that, you know it was special.
Sully texted me 'he's fine' about 15 times. When Sully says someone's fine, start writing the obituary.
